S67.01.needs: a plan that includes managed environments, a GitHub account with a connected repository
S67.01.note: Free-form chat with the agent; there is no separate control for this feature.
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Code.
Tap New session, choose the repository under Where it runs, and make sure a folder is picked.
In the box Describe a task or ask a question, type: Explain this repository's structure: main parts, entry points, and how they fit.
Tap send and wait for the reply to finish.
Compare the reply with Expected: it should name main parts, entry points and how they connect.
S67.01.where: AGI Code > New session > Describe a task or ask a question

S67.10.needs: a cloud session with a repository and a plan that includes managed environments
S67.10.note: The phone runs a command directly; asking the agent in chat to run the tests is the other route.
steps: Open AGI Code and tap an existing cloud session with a repository.
Tap the branch icon in the top bar (labelled Changes).
Scroll down to the Commands section.
Type the repository's test command in Run a command, then tap Run.
Compare with Expected: the output should show the test result.
S67.10.where: AGI Code > open a cloud session > Changes > Commands > Run a command

Tap send and wait until the turn finishes.
Compare with Expected: the reply should explain the failure and the fix should appear in Changes.

S67.24.needs: a cloud session where the phone sets the mode, and a plan that includes managed environments
S67.24.note: Mode is shown only when the environment has no own agent (turnControls = runtimeId null); otherwise the sheet says This environment runs its own agent and manages its mode. The proposal is a chat reply, not a patch with its own review step.
steps: Open a cloud session and tap Task options and usage in the composer.
Under Mode, tap Plan (it says it reads the code and proposes changes without making any).
Close the options, type a change request in Describe a task or ask a question, and tap send.
Tap the branch icon in the top bar (Changes) to see the proposed diff.
Compare with Expected: the proposal should be shown before or without any file being changed.
S67.24.where: AGI Code > open a cloud session > Task options and usage > Mode > Plan

S67.25.needs: a cloud session with a repository and changed files
S67.25.note: The phone selects files to commit; it does not accept or reject individual agent patches before the agent edits.
steps: Open a cloud session that has changed files and tap the branch icon in the top bar (Changes).
Untick the files you do not want under Include in the commit:, leaving only the ones you choose.
Type a message in Commit message and tap Commit and push.
Compare with Expected: only the ticked files are committed and the sheet says Commits X of Y changed files.
S67.25.where: AGI Code > open a cloud session > Changes > Include in the commit: > Commit and push

S67.31.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account, and an open AGI Code session with a repository and working branch
S67.31.note: The button is disabled with a message when the session has no repository or branch or is closed or archived, and it is replaced by the pull request link once one exists.
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Code. The sessions list opens.
Tap a session that has a repository and a working branch and is not closed or archived.
Tap the branch icon at the top right of the session. The sheet titled Changes opens.
Scroll to the Create pull request button and tap it once. Nothing asks you to confirm first.
Look for a pull request link and checks status in the same sheet, and for the link in the session header, then compare with Expected: a pull request should exist on the code host.
S67.31.where: Side menu > AGI Code > open a session > Changes (branch icon, top right) > Create pull request
